description: The physics of motion and forces. Covers Newtonian mechanics, energy, momentum, rotational dynamics, oscillations, gravitation, and the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations.

modules.title: Kinematics in One and Two Dimensions

concepts.title: Position, Velocity, and Acceleration
learning_objectives: Define position, displacement, velocity, and acceleration as derivatives of position with respect to time
Derive kinematic equations for constant acceleration from integration
Interpret position-time, velocity-time, and acceleration-time graphs

concepts.title: Projectile Motion
learning_objectives: Decompose projectile motion into independent horizontal and vertical components
Derive equations for range, maximum height, and time of flight
Solve projectile problems with non-zero launch height and angled surfaces

concepts.title: Relative Motion and Reference Frames
learning_objectives: Apply Galilean velocity addition for objects in different reference frames
Solve problems involving relative velocity in one and two dimensions
Distinguish between inertial and non-inertial reference frames

concepts.title: Curvilinear Motion and Polar Coordinates
learning_objectives: Express velocity and acceleration in polar coordinates (radial and tangential components)
Analyze circular motion using angular velocity and centripetal acceleration
Derive the acceleration vector in polar coordinates: a = (r̈ − rθ̇²)r̂ + (rθ̈ + 2ṙθ̇)θ̂

concepts.title: Newton's Three Laws
learning_objectives: State Newton's three laws of motion and identify the physical content of each
Distinguish between mass and weight and between contact and field forces
Draw free-body diagrams for systems of interacting objects

concepts.title: Applications of Newton's Second Law
learning_objectives: Apply F = ma to solve problems involving friction, normal forces, and tension
Analyze systems with multiple objects connected by strings or in contact
Solve inclined plane problems with and without friction

concepts.title: Circular Motion and Centripetal Force
learning_objectives: Apply Newton's second law to uniform circular motion problems
Analyze banked curves, vertical loops, and conical pendulums
Distinguish between centripetal acceleration and centrifugal effects in rotating frames

concepts.title: Drag Forces and Velocity-Dependent Forces
learning_objectives: Model linear and quadratic drag forces and solve the resulting ODEs
Derive terminal velocity from the force balance condition
Analyze motion with drag in both horizontal and vertical contexts

concepts.title: Work and Kinetic Energy
learning_objectives: Define work as a line integral W = ∫F·dr for a variable force
Derive and apply the work-energy theorem: W_net = ΔKE
Calculate work done by gravity, spring forces, and friction

concepts.title: Potential Energy and Conservative Forces
learning_objectives: Define potential energy for conservative forces and derive U from F = −∇U
Verify that a force is conservative using the curl test
Construct energy diagrams and identify equilibrium points from U(x)

concepts.title: Conservation of Energy
learning_objectives: Apply conservation of mechanical energy to closed systems
Incorporate non-conservative forces (friction, drag) using the work-energy theorem
Solve problems combining gravitational and elastic potential energy

concepts.title: Linear Momentum and Impulse
learning_objectives: Define linear momentum and state Newton's second law as F = dp/dt
Compute impulse as J = ∫F dt and apply the impulse-momentum theorem
Analyze force-time graphs to determine impulse

concepts.title: Conservation of Momentum and Collisions
learning_objectives: Apply conservation of momentum to isolated systems
Analyze elastic and perfectly inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions
Use conservation of energy in conjunction with momentum for elastic collisions

concepts.title: Center of Mass and Rocket Propulsion
learning_objectives: Calculate the center of mass of discrete and continuous mass distributions
Apply Newton's second law to the center of mass of a system
Derive the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation from conservation of momentum

concepts.title: Rotational Kinematics
learning_objectives: Define angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration
Derive rotational kinematic equations analogous to linear kinematics
Relate angular and linear quantities (v = rω, a_t = rα)

concepts.title: Moment of Inertia
learning_objectives: Calculate moment of inertia for discrete and continuous mass distributions using integration
Apply the parallel-axis theorem to find moment of inertia about shifted axes
Compute moments of inertia for standard shapes (rod, disk, sphere, cylinder)

concepts.title: Torque and Rotational Dynamics
learning_objectives: Define torque as τ = r × F and apply Newton's second law for rotation τ = Iα
Analyze rolling motion (rolling without slipping) combining translation and rotation
Solve problems involving pulleys, wheels, and gears with rotational inertia

concepts.title: Angular Momentum and Its Conservation
learning_objectives: Define angular momentum L = r × p for a particle and L = Iω for rigid bodies
Apply conservation of angular momentum to collisions and variable-inertia systems
Analyze precession qualitatively using the torque-angular momentum relation τ = dL/dt

concepts.title: Simple Harmonic Motion
learning_objectives: Derive the SHM equation ẍ + ω²x = 0 from Hooke's law and solve it
Identify amplitude, frequency, period, and phase of SHM
Analyze energy oscillation between kinetic and potential in SHM

concepts.title: Damped Oscillations
learning_objectives: Derive and solve the damped oscillator equation ẍ + 2γẋ + ω₀²x = 0
Classify motion as underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped
Calculate the quality factor Q and relate it to energy dissipation rate

concepts.title: Forced Oscillations and Resonance
learning_objectives: Solve the forced oscillator equation with sinusoidal driving
Derive the steady-state amplitude and phase as functions of driving frequency
Analyze resonance curves and the effect of damping on resonance peak width

concepts.title: Coupled Oscillations and Normal Modes
learning_objectives: Set up the equations of motion for coupled oscillators as a matrix eigenvalue problem
Find normal mode frequencies and mode shapes from the eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Express general motion as a superposition of normal modes

concepts.title: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
learning_objectives: State Newton's law of gravitation and compute gravitational force between two masses
Derive gravitational acceleration g at the surface and at altitude
Apply the shell theorem for spherically symmetric mass distributions

concepts.title: Gravitational Potential Energy and Orbits
learning_objectives: Derive gravitational potential energy U = −GMm/r from the force law
Calculate escape velocity from energy conservation
Apply energy and angular momentum conservation to classify orbits (bound vs unbound)

concepts.title: Kepler's Laws and Orbital Mechanics
learning_objectives: Derive Kepler's three laws from Newton's law of gravitation and angular momentum conservation
Relate orbital parameters (semi-major axis, eccentricity, period) to energy and angular momentum
Calculate orbital transfers (Hohmann transfer) using energy conservation

concepts.title: Accelerating and Rotating Reference Frames
learning_objectives: Derive the transformation of acceleration between inertial and non-inertial frames
Identify and compute centrifugal and Coriolis fictitious forces in a rotating frame
Apply effective gravity in a rotating frame (e.g., variation of g with latitude)

concepts.title: Applications of Non-Inertial Frames
learning_objectives: Analyze the Foucault pendulum as evidence of Earth's rotation
Explain weather patterns (cyclones, trade winds) using the Coriolis effect
Solve projectile problems on a rotating Earth with Coriolis corrections

concepts.title: The Inertia Tensor
learning_objectives: Define the inertia tensor as a 3×3 symmetric matrix
Calculate components of the inertia tensor for continuous and discrete mass distributions
Find principal axes and principal moments of inertia by diagonalizing the inertia tensor

concepts.title: Euler's Equations of Rigid Body Motion
learning_objectives: Derive Euler's equations for torque-free rotation in the body frame
Analyze stable and unstable rotation about principal axes (tennis racket theorem)
Solve Euler's equations for symmetric and asymmetric tops

concepts.title: Generalized Coordinates and Constraints
learning_objectives: Identify degrees of freedom and choose generalized coordinates for constrained systems
Distinguish between holonomic and non-holonomic constraints
Express kinetic and potential energy in terms of generalized coordinates

concepts.title: The Euler-Lagrange Equations
learning_objectives: Define the Lagrangian L = T − U and derive the Euler-Lagrange equations from Hamilton's principle
Apply the Euler-Lagrange equations to mechanical systems (pendulum, bead on wire, Atwood machine)
Identify cyclic coordinates and their associated conserved quantities

concepts.title: Symmetries and Conservation Laws (Noether's Theorem)
learning_objectives: State Noether's theorem relating continuous symmetries to conservation laws
Derive conservation of energy from time-translation symmetry
Derive conservation of linear and angular momentum from spatial symmetries

concepts.title: The Hamiltonian and Hamilton's Equations
learning_objectives: Define the Hamiltonian via the Legendre transform H = Σ pᵢq̇ᵢ − L
Derive Hamilton's canonical equations: q̇ᵢ = ∂H/∂pᵢ, ṗᵢ = −∂H/∂qᵢ
Apply Hamilton's equations to solve simple mechanical systems

concepts.title: Phase Space and Liouville's Theorem
learning_objectives: Represent the state of a system as a point in phase space (q, p)
Draw and interpret phase space trajectories for simple systems (SHM, pendulum)
State Liouville's theorem on the incompressibility of phase space flow

concepts.title: Poisson Brackets
learning_objectives: Define the Poisson bracket {f, g} and compute it for dynamical variables
Express Hamilton's equations using Poisson brackets: ḟ = {f, H}
Identify constants of motion from vanishing Poisson brackets with the Hamiltonian

concepts.title: Postulates and Lorentz Transformations
learning_objectives: State Einstein's two postulates of special relativity
Derive the Lorentz transformation equations from the postulates
Apply Lorentz transformations to relate space and time coordinates between inertial frames

concepts.title: Time Dilation, Length Contraction, and Simultaneity
learning_objectives: Derive and apply the time dilation formula Δt = γΔt₀
Derive and apply the length contraction formula L = L₀/γ
Explain and compute the relativity of simultaneity

concepts.title: Relativistic Momentum and Energy
learning_objectives: Define relativistic momentum p = γmv and relativistic kinetic energy
Derive and apply the energy-momentum relation E² = (pc)² + (mc²)²
Solve collision and decay problems using relativistic conservation laws

concepts.title: Four-Vectors and Spacetime
learning_objectives: Define the spacetime interval and classify events as timelike, spacelike, or lightlike
Construct four-vectors (position, momentum, force) and compute Lorentz-invariant quantities
Apply four-momentum conservation to relativistic collision problems

projects.title: Simulating the Three-Body Problem
projects.description: Numerically integrate the equations of motion for three gravitationally interacting bodies. Explore different initial conditions and identify chaotic behavior, stable configurations, and Lagrange points.
learning_objectives: Set up the coupled ODEs for N gravitating bodies
Implement a numerical integrator (e.g., Runge-Kutta) and analyze energy conservation
Identify sensitivity to initial conditions as a signature of chaos

projects.title: Analyzing a Gyroscope with Lagrangian Mechanics
projects.description: Derive the equations of motion for a symmetric spinning top using Euler angles and the Lagrangian. Analyze precession, nutation, and the sleeping top condition.
learning_objectives: Define and apply Euler angles as generalized coordinates for a rigid body
Derive equations of motion from the Lagrangian with cyclic coordinates
Analyze the qualitative behavior of gyroscopic precession and nutation

projects.title: Relativistic Particle Collider Analysis
projects.description: Analyze particle collision data using relativistic kinematics. Compute center-of-mass energies, threshold energies for particle production, and apply four-momentum conservation to reconstruct invariant masses.
learning_objectives: Transform between lab and center-of-mass frames using Lorentz boosts
Compute threshold energies for particle creation reactions
Reconstruct invariant mass from decay product momenta
